lastCompletedStory.title: WARNING: US-004's byte ceiling does not bound the log while it is being written…

nextStoryContext: US-R1-004 fixed the WARNING that US-004's config-pane debug log byte ceiling (buildConfigLogCapCommand, src/commands/setup.ts) only rotated once at EOF (post-hoc trim: `cat >> LOG; tail -c N LOG > LOG.tmp && mv ...`), so the file grew unbounded for the entire live pipe session (tmux pipe-pane only closes the pipe when the viewer pane exits) -- exactly the 'unbounded, unrotated' defect the original US-004 story was supposed to close. Fix: replaced the single blocking `cat >>` with a streaming rotate loop that reads bounded 4096-byte chunks via `dd` and rotates (tail -c CEILING) after EVERY chunk it appends, so the on-disk file is bounded to `ceiling + one chunk` at any instant during the live session, not just after the pipe closes. buildConfigLogCleanupCommand was also extended to remove the new `.chunk` scratch sibling on EXIT-trap cleanup (a new artifact my own fix introduces; leaving it unremoved would reproduce a smaller instance of the exact leak class CAM-510 exists to close). Quoting constraint discovered and documented in patterns.md: this command text passes through THREE nested shell-parse layers (the menu script's own double-quoted split-window argument, tmux's real single-quote extraction of the pipe-pane -o value, and pipe-pane's own fresh `$SHELL -c` invocation of the extracted text), so it must contain ZERO quote characters of either kind -- used `(( expr ))` arithmetic instead of `[ "$x" -gt N ]` and real embedded newlines instead of `;`-joined statements to stay quote-free. Verified BSD dd (macOS, the dev machine's actual dd, confirmed via `man dd`: no GNU-only `status=`/`iflag=fullblock`, and BSD dd aggregates short reads up to `bs` before writing, unlike GNU's single-read passthrough) behaves correctly under the new construction -- all 8 existing + 1 new test in test/setup-config-log.test.ts pass under the real local dd. Added a new regression test (`keeps the log bounded WHILE still being written`) that spawns the real generated bash command, writes to its stdin in a loop, and samples the on-disk file size BETWEEN writes (mid-stream, before stdin.end()) -- proven non-tautological by running the identical harness against the OLD post-hoc-trim construction, which let the observed size climb to the full unbounded total (20000 bytes) instead of staying near the 2000-byte ceiling; this is the only way to falsify the 'bounded during the live session' property, since every pre-existing test in that file only ever inspected the file AFTER the bash subprocess (and therefore the pipe) had already closed. file-size-budget.json raised for src/commands/setup.ts 954->978 with a dated US-R1-004/CAM-510 _ref note. All quality gates green: typecheck 0 errors, full bun test 6096 pass / 0 fail (+1 from the new regression test, up from the 6095 baseline recorded in the prior handoff), full bun run check:all spine green (file-size, debt-markers, coverage, dead-code, dup, ci-parity, agents-md, test-sleeps -- the new fixed-interval setTimeout in the new test was deliberately cited with a same-line CAM-510 tracker-ref comment since it's a metronomic sampling cadence, not a poll-for-condition wait, so waitForCondition does not apply there -- test-tmpdir all clean). No vendor/templates changes, no embed-vendor needed. This closes the last of the 5 US-004-adjacent CAM-510 follow-up findings raised against this branch's own prior work (US-R1-001 through US-R1-004); the CAM-513 flaky-test-isolation open question from US-R1-003 remains open on main, unrelated to this story's diff.
